# Cold email list gate

The list breaks before deliverability does. A bad filter reaches 20,000 inboxes before anyone notices; ten rows read before load catch it while the fix is still one query change.

## Confirm the job

- You need three inputs: the list (rows or CSV), the ICP definition, and the query or provider that built it.
- No ICP definition means fit cannot be judged. Check mailbox validity only, return INCONCLUSIVE, and ask for the missing definition rather than guessing.
- Sends already happened → hand the case to `cold-email-ops` for an audit. This skill gates before load only.
- Buying, scraping, or enriching contacts → out of scope. Stop and say so.

## Gate the list

1. Sample 10 rows at random before the full list loads. Read each as a prospect: right company, right title, right size, real mailbox. Record the row itself, not a summary.
2. Two or more wrong in ten → HOLD. Fix the query or provider; do not patch individual rows, because patching hides the bad filter.
3. One wrong in ten → GO with the row named in the report. Zero or one is tolerable; two is a pattern.
4. Re-run a fresh 10-row sample after the fix. A HOLD is never lifted on the old sample.
5. Name the common fail pattern: wrong filter, stale source, wrong seniority, invalid mailboxes. The pattern tells the owner what to change.

## Compare providers when that is the question

- Same criteria, 50–100 contacts per provider, not the full list.
- Email: valid-contact rate. Phone: dials to reach one in-profile person.
- Attribute differences to the provider, not to copy or infrastructure. The same criteria can move valid contacts sharply across providers.

## Decide and report

Use the template in `references/gate-rules.md`. The first line is GO or HOLD. Include the 10-row table (#, company, title, size fit, mailbox valid, note), the fail pattern and its cause, and the specific change that triggers a fresh sample. Never invent rows. If the list has fewer than 10 rows, sample all of them and mark the gate INCONCLUSIVE.

## Boundaries

- Copy writing or rewriting → `wordsmith`.
- Post-send diagnosis, capacity, deliverability, or automation → `cold-email-ops`.
- Acquisition, enrichment, and sending → out of scope.

file.content:
# Gate rules and report template

Thresholds come from one operator's account:

> Will Breton (@bretonwill), "Everything I Learned From Managing 3.5M+ Cold Emails/Month",
> X article, 18 October 2026.

The 10-row sample and the "2 wrong means the list is wrong" rule are his. The 50–100
contact provider sample is an adaptation: the source compared phone providers on dials
per in-profile person, not email valid-contact rate. Treat all of it as a starting
threshold, not a law, and label borrowed figures "source benchmark" in the gate report.

| Rule | Value | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-load sample | 10 rows, random | Source: open 10 rows before anything loads |
| HOLD | 2 or more wrong in 10 | Source: if 2 of 10 are off, the whole list has a problem |
| GO | 0 or 1 wrong in 10 | Derived from the HOLD rule; name the one bad row |
| Provider comparison | 50–100 contacts per provider | Adaptation; same criteria, sample only |
| Email provider metric | Valid-contact rate | Adaptation of the source's phone metric |
| Phone provider metric | Dials per in-profile person | Source: 50 dials fell to ~15 on the same criteria with a different provider |
| No ICP | INCONCLUSIVE | Fit cannot be judged; mailbox validity alone is not a gate |
| Fewer than 10 rows | INCONCLUSIVE | Sample every row and say the sample is short |

## Row rubric

- **Company** — exists, matches the ICP's industry and geography.
- **Title** — matches the buying role, not just any employee.
- **Size** — headcount or revenue band matches the ICP.
- **Mailbox** — a real, deliverable address; a pattern that only looks valid is a fail.

A row fails if any one check fails. Record the failing check, not just "bad".

## Gate report template

```
Decision: GO | HOLD | INCONCLUSIVE
List: <name>   Rows: <count>   Sampled: <count>   Date: <date>   Reviewer: <name>

| # | Company | Title | Size fit | Mailbox valid | Note |
|---|---------|-------|----------|---------------|------|

Fail pattern: <wrong filter | stale source | wrong seniority | invalid mailboxes | none>
Cause: <the query, provider, or enrichment step that produced it>
Required change: <specific fix>
Re-run condition: <fresh 10-row sample after the change>

Source benchmarks used: <rules taken from the article, labeled as such>
```

A HOLD is a verdict on the list, not on the offer, the market, or the sender.

content.text:
**Decision: HOLD**

List: provider A, 2,400 rows. Sampled 10 (the supplied sample, so I can't confirm it was random). Date: 2026-11-13.

| # | Company | Title | Size fit | Mailbox valid | Note |
|---|---------|-------|----------|---------------|------|
| 1 | Ledgerline | VP Customer Success | 180, yes | yes | Pass |
| 2 | Quillbook | Head of CS | 95, yes | yes | Pass |
| 3 | Fernway | Customer Success Manager | 240, yes | yes | **Fail: wrong seniority.** ICP needs VP, Head, Director or CCO. |
| 4 | Paystack Labs | none (first name "Info") | 320, yes | **no** | **Fail: role inbox** (info@). |
| 5 | Tallyhub | Director of CS | 410, yes | yes | **Fail: current customer**, excluded in the ICP. |
| 6 | Docket | CCO | **2,600** | yes | **Fail: size.** The ICP cap is 500. |
| 7 | Brightline Talent | Head of CS | 60 | yes | **Fail: recruitment agency**, excluded. |
| 8 | Ravelin Data | VP Customer Experience | 130, yes | **no** | **Fail: gmail address.** The company domain is raveldata.example, and the title is also off-spec. |
| 9 | Stackwise | Head of CS | 75, yes | yes | Pass |
| 10 | Penny Lane Software | Director of CS | 220, yes | yes | Pass |

6 of 10 are wrong. The HOLD threshold is 2 or more.

**Fail pattern:** wrong filter. The failures are spread across title seniority, a size ceiling, exclusions (agency, existing customer) and mailbox type. That points to a query that isn't applying the ICP constraints, not one bad data source. Mailbox quality is a secondary problem (a role inbox and a free-mail address).

**Cause:** provider A's query doesn't enforce the 50–500 size band, the seniority floor, the agency and customer exclusions, or the named-work-address requirement.

**Required change:**
- Cap headcount at 500.
- Restrict titles to VP, Head, Director or CCO of Customer Success.
- Exclude agencies and recruiters by industry.
- Suppress Brightfold and Tallyhub.
- Drop role inboxes and free-mail domains.

**Re-run condition:** pull a fresh random 10-row sample after the fix. A HOLD isn't lifted on this sample. I'd also have provider A re-quote the 2,400 count, because the filters will shrink it.

**Provider B:** the README only gives a summary (8 on ICP, 1 role inbox, 1 over 500 employees), not the rows. That is 2 wrong in 10, which is also HOLD by the same rule. It is still much better than A's 4 on ICP. Before treating B as the fallback, I'd request its actual rows and a 50–100 contact comparison against A on the same criteria. I'm not scoring B from a summary.

**Source benchmarks used:** the 10-row sample and the "2 wrong means HOLD" rule come from Will Breton's X article of 18 October 2026. Treat them as a starting threshold, not a law.
